observations: Photo 0 shows a used black automotive alternator with a visible label reading VALEO and other partially legible text.
Photo 1 shows the side of the alternator with exposed copper windings through cooling vents.
Photo 2 shows the pulley end and opposite side with more windings visible.
The unit appears dusty and grime-covered, consistent with a removed part.

claims.evidence: photo 0 label reads VALEO; photos show an alternator
engine compatibility cannot be confirmed from photos alone
part number on the label is not clearly legible in the photos
origin and prior use cannot be verified from photos

risks.risk: Internal electrical failure (stator, rotor, diode pack, regulator)
risks.proof: bench test video showing charging output
video of the pulley rotating smoothly by hand or motor
clear, legible photo of the full label showing the part number

risks.risk: Physical damage to pulley, mounting ears, or electrical connector
risks.proof: close-up photos of all mounting points and the connector

proof_requests: Clear, well-lit photo of the full label showing brand and part number
Video of the alternator being bench-tested for output voltage
Video of the pulley rotating smoothly without noise or play
response.reason: The photos show a used Valeo car alternator, so it can be priced at its worst case as non-working; compatibility and function remain unproven.
